line: I can never decide at places like this. What are you leaning toward?
followUps: Is that your usual kind of order, or a gamble?
What made that one jump out?
shareBack: Say what you're torn between in one sentence, then ask which they'd pick for you.
deliveryCue: Say it while you're both still looking at the menu.

line: I like this place already. Have you been here before, or is it new to you too?
followUps: What brought you here the first time?
What kind of places do you usually end up at?
shareBack: Mention one thing you noticed walking in, then ask what caught their eye.

line: I always order the same thing and then wish I'd been braver. Are you a try-something-new person?
followUps: What's the best gamble you've made on a menu?
Is there anything you'd never order?
shareBack: Name your safe order in a few words, then ask what they think you should try instead.

line: What's the best thing you've eaten lately?
followUps: Where was that?
Did you find it yourself, or did someone take you there?
shareBack: Offer one good meal of your own in a sentence, then ask if they'd try it.

line: What does a really good weekend look like for you?
followUps: When did you last get one like that?
What's the part you'd never skip?
shareBack: Describe your own good weekend in one sentence, then ask which part they'd join in on.

line: I need something new to watch. Have you seen anything good lately?
followUps: What did you like about it?
Is that the kind of thing you usually go for?
shareBack: Mention the last thing you enjoyed watching, then ask if they've seen it.

line: You seem like someone with strong opinions about dessert.
followUps: So what's the right answer here?
Share one, or one each?
shareBack: Admit your own dessert weakness in a few words, then let them decide for the table.
deliveryCue: Say it with a smile, as a guess, not a verdict.

line: Found any good spots around here lately? I'm always looking for new ones.
followUps: What makes a place a keeper for you?
How did you come across it?
shareBack: Offer one spot you like and why in a sentence, then ask if it sounds like their kind of place.

line: You picked a great spot. How did you find it?
followUps: What do you usually get here?
Do you have a few places like this up your sleeve?
shareBack: Say one thing you like about the place, then ask what they'd show you next.
deliveryCue: Only if they chose the place.

line: What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made that stand out?
Is that a regular thing or a one-off?
shareBack: Give your own small highlight in one sentence, then ask what they've got coming up.

line: What's something you've gotten into lately that you didn't expect to like?
followUps: How did that start?
What keeps you coming back to it?
shareBack: Mention one thing that surprised you the same way, then ask if they'd give it a go.

line: What's the best trip you've taken, even a short one?
followUps: What made it so good?
Would you go back, or was it a one-time thing?
shareBack: Share one trip of yours in a sentence with one detail, then ask where they'd go next.

line: It sounded like a full week. What took up most of it?
followUps: Was that the good kind of busy?
What would have made it easier?
shareBack: Offer one thing that filled your own week, briefly, then ask what they want from the weekend.
deliveryCue: Listen first; don't jump in with fixes.

line: I keep thinking about that place we went last time. Where should we try next?
followUps: What was your favorite part of last time?
Is there somewhere you've been saving up?
shareBack: Say what you liked most about last time in one sentence, then let them choose.

line: Settle something for me: is it ever okay to order for the whole table?
followUps: Has anyone ever done it well for you?
What would you order for us right now?
shareBack: Give your own verdict in a few words, then ask what other food rules they hold.
deliveryCue: Keep it light; you're teasing, not testing.

line: You're in charge of the music. What are we listening to?
followUps: How did you get into them?
Is this your driving music or your everything music?
shareBack: Name one thing you've had on repeat, then ask if it would make their playlist.

line: Anything you're looking forward to in the next few weeks?
followUps: What are you most excited about with that?
How did that come about?
shareBack: Offer one thing you're looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask another question.

line: I'm happy to wander. Is there anything around here you've been wanting to check out?
followUps: What made you curious about it?
Are you a planner or a see-what-happens person?
shareBack: Point out one thing nearby that caught your eye, then ask which way they'd go.

line: What's a small thing that reliably makes your day better?
followUps: How did you figure that out?
When did you last get to do it?
shareBack: Share your own small thing in one sentence, then ask if they'd add it to their list.

line: Looking forward to tonight. Anything you're in the mood for, food-wise?
followUps: Anything you'd rather steer clear of?
Do you want to pick, or should I?
shareBack: Say what you're in the mood for in a few words and leave the final choice open.
deliveryCue: Send it a few hours ahead, not at the last minute.

line: Quick question before we plan anything: coffee and a walk, or a real sit-down dinner?
followUps: Is there a place you already like for that?
Which day suits you best?
shareBack: Say which one you'd lean toward and why in a few words, then let them decide.

line: I had a really good time tonight. Did you get home okay?
followUps: What was your favorite part?
Would you be up for doing it again?
shareBack: Name one moment you enjoyed in a sentence, then leave room for theirs.
deliveryCue: Send it the same evening; keep it short.

line: Something today reminded me of that story you told, and I'm still laughing about it.
followUps: Has anything topped it since?
What are you up to later this week?
shareBack: Say in a few words what set off the memory, then ask when you can hear the next one.
deliveryCue: Needs no long reply; a laugh back is enough.

line: Two ideas for Saturday: something outdoors or somewhere cozy. Which sounds better?
followUps: Morning or evening?
Anything you've been wanting to try?
shareBack: Say which one you're quietly hoping for, then leave the choice with them.

line: Send me a song you've had on repeat. I need something new for the drive.
followUps: Where did you first hear it?
What else should I listen to after this?
shareBack: Send one song back with a few words on why you like it, and ask what they think.

line: I'm picking up coffee on the way. What's your order?
followUps: Is that your everyday order or a treat?
Anything to eat with it?
shareBack: Tell them your own order in a few words when you hand theirs over, and ask how you did.

line: Hope today went the way you wanted. Tell me about it when we're together?
followUps: What was the best part?
What would make tonight a good end to it?
shareBack: Offer one line about your own day only after hearing theirs, then ask about tomorrow.
deliveryCue: Use when you know they had something on today.

line: Your front garden looks great this year. What did you plant along the edge?
followUps: Is it a lot of work to keep up?
Where do you get your plants?
shareBack: Mention one thing you're trying, or failing, to grow, then ask what they'd suggest.

line: Looks like you've got a project going out front. What are you building?
followUps: Are you doing it all yourself?
How long do you think it'll take?
shareBack: Mention a job you keep putting off at your place, then ask how they got started.

line: I don't think we've properly met. I'm a few doors down. How long have you been on the street?
followUps: What do you like most about living here?
Has it changed much in that time?
shareBack: Say how long you've been here in a few words, then ask what you should know about the street.

line: Do you have a go-to place around here for takeout? We're stuck in a rut.
followUps: What do you usually order there?
Is there anywhere you'd tell us to skip?
shareBack: Name the place you order from too often, then ask if they've tried it.

line: Any plans for the weekend, or are you just glad to be home?
followUps: Is that something you do often?
What would the perfect version of it look like?
shareBack: Offer one thing on your own weekend list, in a sentence, then ask another question.

line: I'm heading to the hardware store later. Need anything while I'm there?
followUps: What are you working on at the moment?
Have you found a good place for that kind of thing?
shareBack: Say what job is sending you there in a few words, then ask if they've tackled the same thing.

line: Do you know what they're building down the road? I keep wondering.
followUps: What would you like to see go in there?
Has much else changed around here lately?
shareBack: Share your own guess or hope for it in a sentence, then ask what the street is missing.

line: That wind last night was something. Did everything hold up on your side?
followUps: Did it keep you up?
Do you need a hand with any of it?
shareBack: Mention one thing that blew over or leaked at your place, then offer help if they need it.
deliveryCue: Only after weather that actually did something.

line: We finally tried that new place up the road. Have you been yet?
followUps: What did you think of it?
Where do you usually go instead?
shareBack: Give your verdict in one sentence with one detail, then ask what else is worth trying nearby.

line: Do you know many people here, or are you meeting everyone like I am?
followUps: How do you know the hosts?
Who should I make sure to say hello to?
shareBack: Say who you know here in a few words, then ask how they ended up coming.

line: Have you tried any of the food yet? I need a recommendation.
followUps: What should I go for first?
Did you bring something yourself?
shareBack: Report back on what you tried in a sentence, then ask what they like to make or bring.

line: How's the house project going? Last I heard you were in the thick of it.
followUps: What's been the hardest part?
What's left before you can call it done?
shareBack: Mention a project of your own that ran long, in a sentence, then ask what they'd do differently.

line: What's changed most on the street since you moved in?
followUps: Is that for better or worse, do you think?
What do you hope stays the same?
shareBack: Share one change you've noticed yourself, briefly, then ask what they'd add to the street.

line: What's been keeping you busy lately, apart from the house?
followUps: How did you get into that?
What's the best part of it?
shareBack: Offer one thing filling your own time, in a sentence with a detail, then hand it back.

line: The new paint color looks really good. How did you settle on it?
followUps: Did you do it yourselves?
Is there more on the list after this?
shareBack: Admit one thing at your place that needs the same treatment, then ask for a tip.

line: It's been so quiet on the street this week. I'm not complaining.
followUps: Has your week been quiet too, or the opposite?
Is everyone away, do you think?
shareBack: Say in a few words what your own week has been like, then ask what they have planned.

line: Are you staying around over the break, or heading somewhere?
followUps: Is that a tradition or something new?
What are you most looking forward to?
shareBack: Share your own plan in one sentence, and offer to keep an eye on their place if they're away.

line: Hi, it's your neighbor from across the street. A package of yours landed on our step. Shall I drop it over?
followUps: When's a good time to bring it by?
Does that happen to you often?
shareBack: Add a friendly line about how deliveries go at your place when you hand it over.

line: We're away this weekend. Could you keep an eye out for deliveries? Happy to return the favor anytime.
followUps: Is there anything we can do for you while you're away next?
Are you around or off somewhere too?
shareBack: Say in a few words where you're off to, and ask if they need anything brought back.

line: Heading to the store in an hour. Need anything?
followUps: Anything else while I'm out?
Are you home this afternoon if I drop it by?
shareBack: Mention what you're going for in a few words, so the offer feels easy to accept.

line: Your garden lights look great from our window. Where did you find them?
followUps: Were they hard to put up?
Are you planning anything else out there?
shareBack: Say what you've been meaning to do with your own yard, then ask what they'd start with.

line: We made far too much soup. Can I bring some over?
followUps: Is tonight good, or tomorrow?
Anything you don't eat that I should know about?
shareBack: Tell them what kind it is in a few words, and ask what they've been cooking lately.

line: Haven't seen you out front in a while and thought of you. Hope all's well over there.
followUps: Are you around this weekend?
Anything we can help with at the moment?
shareBack: If they reply, add one line of your own news and suggest a quick catch-up over the fence.
deliveryCue: Needs no answer; don't follow up if they stay quiet.

line: We're thinking of having a few neighbors over for a drink next weekend. Would you be up for it?
followUps: Does Saturday or Sunday suit you better?
Is there anyone on the street we should make sure to ask?
shareBack: Say it'll be easy and informal in a few words, and ask what they like to drink.

line: Quick one: do you have a plumber or handyman you'd recommend? We need one.
followUps: What did you have them do?
Anyone you'd tell us to avoid?
shareBack: Say what's gone wrong at your place in a few words, and offer your own contacts in return.

line: Is your power out too, or is it just us?
followUps: Have you heard how long it'll be?
Do you need candles or anything?
shareBack: Say what you know so far in one line, and offer to pass on any update you get.

line: Which one out there is yours?
followUps: How long have they been doing this?
Are they enjoying it so far?
shareBack: Point out your own in a few words, then ask how they heard about this group.

line: Is this your first season with this group, or have you been coming a while?
followUps: What made you choose this one?
Anything a newer parent should know?
shareBack: Say how long you've been coming in a few words, then ask what they like about it.

line: The coach has so much patience. I couldn't do it.
followUps: Have you had this coach before?
Have you ever been roped into helping out?
shareBack: Admit in a sentence how you'd cope in charge of that many kids, then ask about them.
deliveryCue: Say it quietly; kids and other parents are in earshot.

line: We're always hunting for things to do with the kids on rainy weekends. Found anything good around here?
followUps: What made that one work so well?
Is it somewhere you'd go back to?
shareBack: Offer one place that worked for your family, in a sentence, then ask if they've tried it.

line: Do you have a full weekend of this, or is today the only one?
followUps: What do you do with the gaps in between?
Does it ever let up?
shareBack: Run through your own weekend schedule in one sentence, then ask what they do to recover.

line: We barely made it on time today. How do you get everyone out the door?
followUps: Does that work every time?
What's the part that always slows you down?
shareBack: Confess the one thing that held you up this morning, then ask for their best trick.

line: How did you end up signing up for this one?
followUps: Did you try anything else first?
Would you sign up again?
shareBack: Say how your family landed here in one sentence, then ask what else they've heard is good.

line: This is a great spot for a party. Have you been here before?
followUps: What else is there to do here?
Have you found other good places for this kind of thing?
shareBack: Mention one party place you've been to, good or bad, then ask where they'd pick.

line: How do you know the birthday family? School, or the neighborhood?
followUps: Have the kids known each other long?
Do you know many of the other parents here?
shareBack: Say how you know the family in a few words, then ask who else you should meet.

line: I'm impressed anyone can host this many kids and stay calm.
followUps: Have you hosted one of these yet?
What's the best kids' party you've been to?
shareBack: Share one short party story of your own, then ask what they'd do differently next time.

line: What are the kids into right now that you didn't see coming?
followUps: How did that start?
Have you been pulled into it too?
shareBack: Offer one surprising craze from your own house, in a sentence, then ask how long theirs has lasted.

line: What do you do with a Saturday when nothing's on the schedule?
followUps: When did you last get one of those?
Is that with the whole family or on your own?
shareBack: Describe your own free Saturday in one sentence, then ask what they'd do with two.

line: What's surprised you most about this stage with the kids?
followUps: Is that easier or harder than the stage before?
What's helped?
shareBack: Share one thing that caught you off guard, in a sentence, then ask what they're enjoying most.
deliveryCue: For a quiet corner, not in front of the kids.

line: Funny seeing you away from the school gate. Out running errands too?
followUps: Is this your usual spot for that?
What's the rest of your day looking like?
shareBack: Say what you're out for in a few words, then ask if they know a better place for it.

line: Are you signing up for anything next season, or taking a break?
followUps: What tipped the decision?
Have you heard good things about any of the others?
shareBack: Say what your family is leaning toward in one sentence, then ask what they'd recommend.

line: The snacks you brought last week were a hit. Where did you get them?
followUps: Is that your go-to for these things?
Any other ideas? My turn is coming up.
shareBack: Admit what you were planning to bring, in a few words, then ask if it'll pass.

line: You seem to know how all this works. Anything I should know about the schedule?
followUps: What catches new families out?
Who's the right person to ask if I get stuck?
shareBack: Say in a few words that you're new to it, thank them, and ask how their first season went.

line: Have you figured out the school break yet? We're still piecing it together.
followUps: Where did you hear about that?
Is there anything you'd do again from last time?
shareBack: Share the one part of your plan that's settled, then ask what they'd suggest for the rest.

line: These early starts are no joke. I'm running on coffee.
followUps: Are you a morning person, or is this painful for you too?
Where do you get your coffee on the way?
shareBack: Say what time your alarm went off, then ask what they're doing once this is over.

line: Is there a good place for coffee near here? I've got an hour to fill.
followUps: Do you usually stay and watch, or head off?
Want me to bring you one back?
shareBack: Say how you usually spend the wait in a few words, then ask what they do with it.

line: Hi, it's one of the parents from the team. Do you know what time we need to be there Saturday?
followUps: Is it the usual place?
Are you all going to make it?
shareBack: Thank them, add one friendly line about your own Saturday, and say you'll see them there.

line: We're driving to practice anyway. Want us to pick yours up on the way?
followUps: What time works for pickup?
Should we bring them home afterward too?
shareBack: Say it's no trouble in a few words, and ask if there's another day you could share the driving.

line: Thanks for the heads-up about the schedule change. You saved our morning.
followUps: Can you make the new time?
How do you keep on top of all the messages?
shareBack: Admit in a line how close you came to turning up at the wrong time, then offer to return the favor.

line: The kids had a great time together today. Should we set up a playdate one weekend?
followUps: Which weekend is easiest for you?
Park, or one of our houses?
shareBack: Offer one or two dates that suit you in a line, and leave the choice of place to them.

line: Are you going to the thing at school on Friday? We're trying to decide if we'll make it.
followUps: Have you been to one before?
Want to meet up there?
shareBack: Say which way you're leaning and why in a few words, then suggest meeting there.

line: Quick question: where did you get the gear for the team? We still need some.
followUps: Was there anything you didn't end up needing?
Did the sizes run true?
shareBack: Say what you've got and what's missing in a line, and thank them for saving you a trip.

line: We're heading to the park after pickup tomorrow if you'd like to join. No pressure either way.
followUps: Is there a park you like better?
Would another day be easier?
shareBack: Add one detail, such as which park or that you'll bring snacks, and leave it open.

line: We haven't crossed paths since the season ended, and I thought of you. Coffee sometime?
followUps: Is a weekday morning or a weekend easier?
Are you signed up for anything this season?
shareBack: If they reply, give one line of your own news and suggest a specific day.
deliveryCue: Keep it short; don't chase if they don't answer.
